newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai brokers discuss B share trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai brokers discuss B share trading.

text.p: Brokers from major securities houses met in Shanghai on Friday to discuss ways to curb domestic investors trading on the foreign currency B share market, sources said.
The meeting was organised by the Shanghai stock exchange with officials from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the top securities watchdog, present, they said.
It focused on the implementation of existing regulations banning domestic investors from trading in the B share market, theoretically reserved for foreign investors, the sources said.

A key issue was the effectiveness of the CSRC's call earlier this year for the re-registration of all domestic B share account holders in order to weed out local investors trading illegally, they added.
They said no new measures affecting B share trading were discussed at the meeting.
Brokers in Shenzhen said they were unaware of plans for a similar meeting to be held there to discuss the issue.
The CSRC set a deadline of end-March for the completion of the re-registration process by all brokerages in Shanghai, but brokers said the process had only had a limited impact on domestic trading.
Brokers estimate that domestic investors now account for at least half of daily B share trading volume on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges.
Under the CSRC's rules, domestic investors are only allowed to trade B shares if they have a document from an overseas resident empowering them to trade on the overseas resident's behalf.
Some brokerage sources this morning said they had expected a meeting of China-wide brokerages to discuss possible new measures to curb domestic investors trading B shares.
